review_type: Source-lead check; not separate formal critical review
reviewer: AI source agent; authored source package, not central numerical implementation
scope: Read the full manuscript, compare source-facing clauses with retained read scope, inspect selected printed targets and execution metadata counts. No numerical rerun.

findings.issue: General nominal-dollar label exceeds verified source price convention.
findings.fix: Model-dollar units; explicit unresolved source price basis.

findings.issue: Original summary-field count was 60 while saved record has 80.
Abstract could confuse fixed aggregate cost with fixed individual benefit.
findings.fix: Abstract now states aggregate floor expenditure.

checks.claim: Identity, April 2026 version and proposed policy package
checks.evidence: F1 title, Sections 2–3
checks.note: The manuscript identifies a public working proposal. It does not claim enactment or verified national effects.

checks.claim: Individual maximum and aggregate floor expense
checks.evidence: F1 Section 2.1 and 3.1; M1 constants; M2 constants
checks.note: The abstract now refers to aggregate floor expenditure. The main text separates $25,000 per person from the $4.62T aggregate assumption and does not validate coverage calibration.

checks.evidence: F1 Section 2.1
checks.note: The favorable fixed-payment interpretation is grounded in explicit source policy language. It is presented as an interpretation.

checks.evidence: M1 lines 154–168; M2 lines 100–108
checks.note: Each year starts from base. The second test uses the first-stage floor. It sets the aggregate to 120% of base, not a compounded second 20% increment.

checks.claim: Strict thresholds, start years, base supplementary/admin denominator and unused threshold parameter
checks.evidence: M1 lines 80–81 and 154–168
checks.note: The manuscript describes the implemented rule and preserves its denominator choice.

checks.claim: Common distributions, seed and path length
checks.evidence: M1 constants, GROWTH_PARAMS and run_simulation; M2 corresponding blocks
checks.note: Common distributions and seed agree. Different horizon lengths change random-stream consumption before the next path. No source-level paired-cohort claim is made.

checks.claim: Meaning of surplus and median consistency
checks.evidence: M1 reducer lines 207–233; M2 reducer lines 131–144
checks.note: Surplus means strictly positive annual gap. The middle order statistic cannot be negative when the positive share exceeds one-half. This is a definition check, not a source model run.

checks.claim: Printed negative median / greater-than-half probability conflict
checks.evidence: F1 abstract, Sections 6.2 and 6.4
checks.note: The exact printed source statements support the manuscript. The difference between a median gap and a difference of medians is handled correctly.

checks.evidence: F3 Whitepaper Numbers That Need Updating, item 1
checks.note: Full note read. It names the older roughly 34% and later 55.7% values. No concealment or intent claim is made.

checks.evidence: logs/search-and-design.json and reviews/feasibility-source-lead.md
checks.note: The paper reports only what the bounded search found. It does not infer novelty from a lack of returned hits.

checks.claim: Source cutoff versus execution and later preparation
checks.evidence: sources/README.md; source-acquisitions.json; reviewer-source-acquisitions.json; protocol-freeze.json; numerical-run-log.json
checks.note: The cutoff concerns bytes acquired by 19:00:03 UTC. The plan was fixed at 18:59:28.032901 UTC. Numerical work began later at 19:02:33.488136 UTC. Preparation and reading can occur after a retrieval cutoff.

checks.evidence: source manifest; snapshots licence notices; vendor licence and migration record
checks.note: Whitepaper copy is unchanged under the stated CC BY 4.0 licence. The scripts are unchanged with MIT notice. No new licence for the original research is selected.

checks.claim: Cost reconstruction and revenue boost description
checks.evidence: M1 returned fields, expense and VAT blocks; M2 expense and VAT blocks
checks.note: The ten-year source exposes the fields stated. The extended source uses a fixed floor and known supplementary/admin formulas. The VAT spending boost does not depend on the floor rule. Generated reconstruction correctness belongs to formal numerical review.

checks.evidence: results/printed-checks.csv versus F1 Sections 6.2 and 6.4
checks.note: All 28 source values and locations were checked against retained F1. The computed columns were not independently reproduced by this source check.

checks.evidence: F1 Section 2.1 and final line; M1–M2 numerical input conventions
checks.note: The paper now calls amounts model dollars and states that it does not resolve the source price basis. Non-indexed payment language alone does not verify that every modeled flow uses a consistent nominal-dollar basis.

checks.claim: Number of saved original summary comparisons
checks.evidence: logs/execution.json original_source_summary_matches
checks.note: Saved metadata has 80 entries, not 60. The frozen paper now says 80. This was a count of saved records, not a model rerun.

checks.evidence: logs/source-stdout-check.json
checks.note: The saved record declares 200 checks and has 200 rows. It limits its scope to baseline tables. This check did not reproduce those numerical comparisons.

checks.evidence: P1 PDF pages 11–16 and 24–26; selected earlier framework pages
checks.note: Guarantee, phase-out, financing and replacement scope are inside the read passages. No full-paper read or reproduction claim is made.

checks.evidence: P2 README, transfer indexation and limitations
checks.note: The README distinguishes fixed and indexed payments and calls its model uncalibrated. The manuscript does not claim to have tested its code.

checks.evidence: P3 Sections 1 and 4, printed pages 3–6 and 11–12
checks.note: The retained note changes benefit amounts or tax rates under fiscal constraints. The manuscript does not claim to reproduce the estimates.

checks.claim: Full work displacement and inference limits
checks.evidence: M1–M2 wage-related revenue and displacement blocks; F1 scope
checks.note: The paper states that these scripts do not model complete loss of human competitiveness. It does not treat simulation frequencies as empirical national probabilities.

checks.claim: Other tax, retirement, legal and welfare questions excluded
checks.evidence: F1 wider scope; acquired-files read-scope ledger
checks.note: The manuscript does not validate the separate models or infer welfare dominance from a smaller deficit. The word private identifies non-government authorship, not private access; the surrounding public-source description is clear.

checks.paper_location: Section 4 numerical estimates, path counts and test outcomes
checks.evidence: Analysis code, generated result files and execution logs
checks.note: The source lead checked the source definitions and selected source transcriptions only. No analysis script was run and no central numerical result was independently recomputed. Separate formal review is still needed.

disposition: No unresolved source-claim blocker within this scope at the repaired hash. This does not close the formal numerical or critical review.
